links.comparator_used: Baseline pipeline (LLM without retrieval) compared with Hybrid biomedical RAG
links.outcome: Exact-code F1 against expert-built reference code sets
links.effect: Hybrid biomedical RAG improved aggregate F1 only for Qwen; GPT-5.5 RxNorm F1 rose from 0.320 to 0.909. Claude and GPT-5.5 had their best aggregate results with Baseline.
links.tradeoff: Retrieval did not consistently improve exact-code performance. Macro-averaged criterion-level gains came with lower micro-averaged aggregate performance.
links.quote: Hybrid biomedical RAG improved aggregate F1 only for Qwen but increased GPT-5.5 RxNorm F1 from 0.320 to 0.909.

links.comparator_used: Staged verifier ablation: candidate codes before verification compared with after existence/vocabulary checking, acceptance filtering, and final verification and expansion
links.effect: Micro-F1 rose from 0.254 before verification to 0.505 after final verification and expansion. Existence/vocabulary checking removed 2,594 false-positive codes, and acceptance filtering removed 952 more.
links.tradeoff: Deterministic verification improves code validity and query readiness but cannot replace accurate clinical interpretation. Overly broad or incomplete candidate generation remained the main source of error.
links.quote: Existence/vocabulary checking removed 2,594 false-positive codes, and acceptance filtering removed 952 additional false-positive codes before controlled expansion.

design_hint: deterministic terminology verification and retrieval grounding of LLM outputs
